source_name: RozetkaPay — marketplace-born PSP (EVO/Rozetka group)
source_subtype: PSP product site (+ parent EVO project page)
why_relevant: Spun out of the Rozetka/EVO marketplace group into a standalone payment service: acquiring across Rozetka, Prom.ua, Bigl.ua, Shafa plus external internet acquiring and BNPL. A structurally distinctive competitor — captive marketplace volume converted into open acquiring.

source_name: NovaPay — Nova Poshta group payment company, API and PRRO integrations
why_relevant: Logistics-group payment company offering internet acquiring and mass payouts, with documented rapid integration into partner POS/cash-register systems and automatic fiscalisation — directly adjacent to POS/fiscalisation vendors. Public developer portal lists integration surface.

source_name: EasyPay — terminal network and online acquiring
why_relevant: Operates a self-service terminal network plus online acquiring — relevant both as a payments competitor and as a hardware/self-service estate operator, which touches POS/kiosk vendor territory.

source_name: plata by mono (Universal Bank / monobank) — acquiring product
why_relevant: monobank's acquiring product spanning internet acquiring, payment links, QR payments and POS terminals — a neobank-native competitor to both PSPs and classic bank acquirers, with an ecosystem play that pressures PSP pricing.

source_name: LiveBusiness UA — internet acquiring service catalogue
why_relevant: Maintained directory/ranking of Ukrainian internet-acquiring and payment-acceptance services — a compact enumeration of the competitive set including smaller players that do not surface in press coverage.

source_name: ApiX-Drive integration catalogue (Ukrainian PSP connectors)
why_relevant: Third-party iPaaS listing hundreds of connectors per PSP (WayForPay, LiqPay, Fondy). The connector lists are a machine-readable map of which CRMs, CMSs and SaaS tools sit around each Ukrainian gateway — i.e. the de-facto partner ecosystem.

source_name: KeyCRM / SITNIKS / Brander and similar integrator blogs and integration pages
why_relevant: Ukrainian CRM/e-commerce software vendors and web agencies document exactly which PSPs they integrate and how, and often name merchant clients — an indirect but rich channel-level view of PSP adoption that PSPs themselves do not publish.

source_name: NBU Payment Infrastructure Register / payment services licensing announcements
why_relevant: Statutory register of licensed payment-service providers plus NBU licensing news (e.g. licences granted to FinPay and WayForPay; ~28 participants entered on the register at time of reporting). The authoritative way to enumerate legitimate PSP competitors and detect new entrants; also the source of the Sept-2025 acquiring rule change requiring a direct acquirer-merchant contract, which reshapes PSP/bank partnership structures.

source_name: Ukrainian bank acquiring product pages (PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen, PUMB, Sense, A-Bank)
why_relevant: Bank acquirers are the counterparties PSPs partner with and compete against; their business-acquiring pages disclose tariffs, terminal offers and named gateway partners, and PrivatBank's terms pages document LiqPay's contractual perimeter.

source_name: PSP LinkedIn company pages (Tranzzo, Fondy, MustPay, NovaPay, RozetkaPay)
why_relevant: Partnership and merchant-win announcements frequently appear on LinkedIn before or instead of the corporate site, and hiring posts signal market expansion. Useful for timing partnership news.

source_name: ensun payment-gateway company index (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Aggregated English-language index claiming ~37 Ukrainian payment-gateway companies — useful purely for enumerating long-tail names to verify elsewhere; the underlying data quality of such aggregators is unverified.

source_name: FinClub (Фінансовий клуб) — Ukrainian banking news & investigations portal
source_subtype: trade media / specialist financial news portal
why_relevant: Specialist Ukrainian banking trade outlet run by ex-banking journalists; covers bank IT/AI implementations, vendor-backed special projects (PUMB, Sense Bank), FinAwards technology rankings, and roundtables such as 'Як штучний інтелект змінює українські банки'. Its /projects and /news streams frequently name the technology and supplier behind a bank initiative.

source_name: FinClub special projects — bank-sponsored technology showcases (PUMB, Sense Bank etc.)
why_relevant: Sponsored/branded sections where banks describe their own digital roadmaps in more detail than in press releases — useful for inferring which vendors and platform choices sit behind a bank's app, but must be read as promotional, not independent.

source_name: Ekonomichna Pravda (Економічна правда) — Finance section
why_relevant: Leading Ukrainian business/investigative outlet. Its finance desk covers bank M&A (Zen.com/PINbank, Crédit Agricole/Lviv Bank), NBU rules on outsourcing and third-party/critical-service contractors — i.e. exactly the regulatory pressure that reshapes bank vendor relationships — and political scandals touching bank governance.

source_name: Forbes Ukraine (forbes.ua)
why_relevant: Covers the largest Ukrainian fintech/banking deals with valuation and shareholder detail (e.g. Fintech-IT Group / monobank developer at $1bn+ with UMAEF), plus company rankings and founder interviews that reveal technology stacks and partner relationships.

source_name: special.ain.ua — AIN branded/vendor special projects
why_relevant: Vendor-funded microsites on AIN carry unusually explicit vendor self-descriptions — e.g. PayForce claiming a multi-module online banking platform integrated with 10+ Ukrainian banks. Promotional, but a rare public statement of an integration footprint.

source_name: Interfax-Ukraine English service (en.interfax.com.ua)
why_relevant: Ukraine's main commercial business wire in English; carries investment/M&A items (e.g. UMAEF–Fintech-IT Group) and a press-release channel where banks, vendors and data firms publish announcements directly. Feeds Bloomberg/Reuters, so items here propagate internationally.

source_name: Interfax-Ukraine press-release channel (paid placement wire)
why_relevant: Paid-placement channel where vendors and banks announce partnerships that never appear as independent news — a low-noise surface for detecting new supplier relationships, provided items are labelled as sponsor-authored.

source_name: Minfin.com.ua — finance portal and bank news aggregator
why_relevant: High-volume Ukrainian consumer-finance portal with continuous bank news, plus a projects arm (project.minfin.com.ua) running the Ukrainian Credit Conference and similar events whose agendas and sponsor lists expose active vendors.

source_name: Banker.ua — Ukrainian banking sector news
why_relevant: Niche banking-community outlet covering appointments, product launches and payment/transfer services; useful for lower-profile bank-vendor items that the large business dailies skip.

source_name: LIGA.net Finance — banking news desk
why_relevant: Major general-news group with a dedicated banking vertical; strong on regulatory and state-bank stories (PrivatBank, Oschadbank) where procurement and IT-modernisation decisions surface.

source_name: SPEKA.media — banking services topic stream
why_relevant: Ukrainian tech/business outlet with a tag page dedicated to banking services; covers product and integration news from a technology angle and often interviews product owners at banks and fintechs.

source_name: Mezha.Media — Ukrainian fintech sector analysis
why_relevant: Tech outlet publishing periodic state-of-the-sector pieces on Ukrainian fintech (trends in cybersecurity, AI, open banking) that name the companies driving each trend — useful as an orientation/pointer layer rather than deal reporting.

source_name: UAFIC — Ukrainian Association of Fintech and Innovative Companies, news & annual catalogue
why_relevant: Industry body whose annual fintech company catalogue (produced with NBU, Ministry of Digital Transformation and IFC support) is effectively a ready-made actor map of ~260 Ukrainian fintech firms, and whose news page announces memoranda and partnerships. Strongest single pointer for expanding the vendor/competitor list feeding the media monitoring.

source_name: Business Censor (censor.net/biz)
why_relevant: Business desk of a large Ukrainian news site with a continuous finance/business feed; useful as a breadth backstop for bank and state-procurement stories that the specialist outlets miss.

source_name: NV Business (biz.nv.ua)
why_relevant: Business arm of NV covering companies, markets and finance; carries bank ownership, management and market-share stories, and runs its own rankings that can be mined for competitive positioning.

source_name: UKR.NET source feeds for financial trade media
why_relevant: Ukraine's dominant news aggregator exposes per-outlet feed pages (PaySpace Magazine, Ekonomichna Pravda and others), giving a single normalised surface to monitor several cell outlets and to recover headlines when an outlet blocks direct crawling.

source_name: DOU.ua company profiles (jobs.dou.ua) as a media/vendor cross-reference
why_relevant: Ukrainian IT-community platform hosting company profiles and reviews for both the trade outlets and the fintech vendors they cover; hiring activity and stack descriptions are an indirect signal of which vendors are actually delivering bank projects.
